passages.note: Bill status page names Kolodin as prime sponsor of HB2785, an omnibus elections bill ('primary; identification; canvass; recounts; ballots') signed into law.

House Third Reading vote page shows Kolodin voting Y on this multi-subject elections bill, passed 56-2; the near-unanimous margin and bundled subjects mean the vote shows no specific identification clause.

passages.provision_quote: Beginning in 2026, aT ANY VOTING LOCATION THE VOTER MAY CHOOSE TO PROVIDE IDENTIFICATION WHEN PRESENTING THE VOTER'S MAILED EARLY BALLOT, AND IF SO THE ELECTION OFFICIAL SHALL: ( a ) REQUIRE THE VOTER TO PRESENT IDENTIFICATION THAT COMPLIES WITH PARAGRAPH 1 OF THIS SUBSECTION.
passages.note: Enacted bill text keeps the existing photo-ID-or-two-document option for in-person voting unchanged and adds only an optional ID check a voter 'may choose' when dropping off a mailed early ballot; this sits alongside unrelated primary-date, canvass and recount provisions in the same instrument.

rows.reasoning: HB2785 (2024) is an omnibus elections bill ('primary; identification; canvass; recounts; ballots') that Kolodin prime-sponsored and voted Y on, but its identification content is only one of several bundled subjects (V4 multi-subject). The identification text itself leaves the existing photo-ID-or-two-document in-person rule untouched and adds only an optional, voter-chosen ID check for mail-ballot drop-off, so no passage matches any rung clause for clause and no tying statement from Kolodin ties the vote or sponsorship to a specific identification provision.
needs_source: A statement or floor explanation from Kolodin tying his sponsorship or vote on HB2785 to a specific identification provision (e.g., the mail-ballot ID option in Sec. 10, 16-579(A)(4)).
